artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for the fourth file_scope_arr splice admitting a touched extension's own manifest.json at both containment sites, with its Site-3 deviation and new fixtures.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a fourth, local, non-declared splice to git-commit-phase.sh's and git-commit-scoped.sh's Containment Self-Checks admitting a touched extension's own manifest.json whenever that extension's scripts/ tree (excluding deprecated/) is also touched, pinned by five new fixtures and documented in git-staging-scope.md.

memory_candidates.content: git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check (Site 2) and git-commit-scoped.sh's own independent V10 containment_scope_arr resolution (Site 3) are two separate, non-shared predicates over the same declared file_scope. Widening only one of them to admit a new path does not make that path land -- Site 3 still drops it, turning what was previously a silent, recoverable drop into a loud post-commit completeness-check failure (exit 6). Any future local widening of the containment predicate must be mirrored identically into both sites.

A structurally-derivable registration obligation (e.g. sync-manifest-scripts.sh's provides.scripts <-> scripts/ tree pairing, enforced by a test) can be admitted into a containment predicate as a pure string derivation over files_touched -- no filesystem/git/jq lookup needed -- keeping the splice fail-open by construction and local to the in-script array only, never written back to the declared file_scope.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh / git-commit-scoped.sh containment sites
sapience_notes.value: The two scripts maintain fully independent containment predicates over the same declared file_scope (Site 2 in git-commit-phase.sh's file_scope_arr, Site 3 in git-commit-scoped.sh's containment_scope_arr). A local widening applied to only one site does not change what lands in a commit -- the other site's independent re-derivation from raw specs/state.json still drops the path.

sapience_notes.subject: Extension manifest.json registration drop from phase commits
sapience_notes.value: sync-manifest-scripts.sh and check-extension-docs.sh's Rule Q already mechanically enforce that an extension's manifest.json provides.scripts entry pair with every file under that extension's scripts/ tree (deprecated/ excluded), post-redeploy. The LIVE failure mode this task fixed was a different one: the manifest.json edit WAS made in the same phase but then dropped by the pre-commit Containment Self-Check as an undeclared scope excursion, costing a separate follow-up commit.

sapience_notes.subject: Task 486 plan premise error (Phase 2)
sapience_notes.value: The plan's Non-Goals assumed a Site-2-only (git-commit-phase.sh) splice would suffice to admit the extension manifest.json into a phase commit. Writing the admit fixture disproved this: Site 2's widening alone turned the pre-existing silent drop-and-warn into a loud post-commit completeness-check failure (exit 6), because git-commit-scoped.sh's Site-3 V10 resolution independently re-reads raw specs/state.json with no knowledge of Site 2's splice.

sapience_notes.subject: Containment fixture design -- collapsed issue-row shape
sapience_notes.value: Task 484's prior work collapsed the Containment Self-Check's per-path scope-excursion issue-record.sh emission into one row per drop event (naming all dropped paths), not one row per path. Any new fixture asserting a genuine out-of-territory drop must assert that collapsed shape, not a per-path shape, or it silently regresses task 484's fix.

sapience_notes.subject: Fold-instead-of-duplicate fixture discipline
sapience_notes.value: When a plan's Scope Hypothesis names a fixture scenario (e.g. trailing-slash directory normalization) that turns out to already be pinned by an existing test case, the correct move is folding the new assertion into that existing case rather than adding a duplicate -- recorded explicitly in the phase's own notes so the fold is traceable.
